blogs.title: Data, Deciphered: Why I'm Building a Bridge Between Business Analysis and AI
blogs.snippet: The role of a Business Analyst has moved beyond static requirements. Discover why converging business logic, financial mathematics, and AI agents forms the future of commercial decisions...
blogs.content:
Introduction

The contemporary business analyst role has undergone a tectonic shift. It is no longer sufficient to merely gather user stories and author static Functional Requirement Documents (FRDs). Today, high-impact enterprise execution demands an intimate bridge between core financial mathematics, operational telemetry, and intelligent automated systems.


Vision: Why This Platform?

I built this space to explore where corporate strategy converges with modern engineering execution. The primary constraint for growing enterprises is rarely a lack of data—it is the velocity with which uncurated transactional data can be converted into defensible executive action.

In this publication series, I document engineering breakdowns across four pivotal vectors:

  • Core Financial & Operational BI: Moving past standard charts into variance decomposition, 13-week rolling liquidity modeling, and contribution margin frameworks.
  • Econometric Pricing Strategy: Employing empirical price elasticity and commodity index modeling to eliminate arbitrary pricing decisions.
  • Edge AI & Retrieval Agents: Grounding Large Language Models on deterministic enterprise rows to answer complex institutional queries sub-second.
  • Full-Stack Analytics Portals: Architecting responsive web telemetry (React, Vite, Supabase, Cloudflare Workers) that replace clunky legacy software.

The Underlying Philosophy: Automate the Mundane, Amplify the Meaningful

Whether tracking multi-subsidiary debt covenants or deploying edge triage bots, the objective remains constant: eliminate systemic friction so leadership teams can focus on strategic capital allocation.

blogs.title: Consolidating Multi-Company Balance Sheets: How We Built a Real-Time CFO Control Suite

The Problem: Fragmented Ledgers & Reconciliation Latency

In multi-entity holding groups and industrial conglomerates, monthly closing is often an ordeal. Each subsidiary runs its own general ledger schema, resulting in 40+ hours of manual reconciliation to answer basic questions: What is our consolidated debt service coverage ratio? Which operating unit is draining working capital?


Architectural Approach: Unified Normalization & Interactive Variance

To solve this, we architected the Strategic Financial Dashboard. Built with a lightweight, zero-bloat web architecture and Chart.js, the system models:

  • Consolidated EBITDA Margins: Dynamic waterfall breakdowns isolating volume, price, and overhead variances across operating subsidiaries.
  • Working Capital Cycles: Real-time tracking of DSO (Days Sales Outstanding), DPO (Days Payable Outstanding), and DIO (Days Inventory Outstanding).
  • Debt Covenant & Solvency Ratios: Visual warning thresholds indicating covenant breach proximity on long-term credit lines.

Quantifiable Impact

By automating the multi-entity consolidation pipeline, month-end financial synthesis was compressed from 5 business days to instant executive inspection with 99.4% audit reconciliation accuracy.

blogs.title: Eliminating Hallucinations: Building a Grounded Edge AI Agent with Groq & Supabase
blogs.snippet: Generative AI without strict grounding is an enterprise liability. We built MisAIAgent using Groq LPU inference, Supabase PostgreSQL rows, and edge functions to achieve deterministic sub-second search...
blogs.content:
The Hallucination Dilemma in Institutional Information Systems

Standard LLM deployments fail in academic departments and corporate intranets because generic foundational models will cheerfully fabricate office locations, course prerequisites, and faculty email addresses when unsure.


The System Architecture: Strict Retrieval-Augmented Grounding

MisAIAgent was constructed under an uncompromising design rule: The model may only formulate answers derived strictly from verified database records.

  • Sub-600ms Inference via Groq: Utilizing Groq's Language Processing Units (LPUs) to execute inference with near-zero token generation latency.
  • Deterministic Supabase Filtering: Queries first parse user intent into structured SQL parameters, pulling target instructor and curriculum records from Supabase PostgreSQL before prompting the LLM.
  • PWA Mobile Client: Fully installable Progressive Web App offering seamless instant search on mobile devices for campus visitors and students.

Takeaways for Enterprise AI Deployments

Context injection with rigid boundary constraints beats fine-tuning for institutional search. It eliminates training drift, safeguards data privacy, and ensures 100% verifiable outputs.

blogs.title: The Mathematics of Pricing: Building an Interactive Price-Elasticity Simulation Cockpit
blogs.snippet: Arbitrary price increases routinely destroy profitability when products cross unit elasticity thresholds. Discover how we built an econometric simulation tool to pinpoint optimal profit maxima (P*)...
blogs.content:
Why Cost-Plus Pricing Destroys Enterprise Value

Most commercial teams employ cost-plus pricing or intuitive gut checks. However, if a product's price elasticity of demand (|E_d|) is greater than 1.0 (elastic), a 10% price hike will precipitate a greater than 10% volume plunge, leading to net gross profit contraction.


Formulating the Interactive Cockpit

The Price Elasticity Cockpit allows commercial analysts to simulate non-linear demand reactions using both constant elasticity models (Q = A * P^epsilon) and linear demand curves (Q = a - bP):

  • Interactive Sensitivity Sliders: Slide baseline volume, unit variable costs, and elasticity parameters to observe real-time profit and revenue trajectories.
  • Identification of P* (Optimal Price): The simulation automatically solves the first derivative of total profit: d(Profit)/dP = 0, surfacing the exact point of maximum gross margin.
  • Consumer Surplus & Deadweight Loss: Visualizes the welfare tradeoff between aggressive extraction and market share volume expansion.

Strategic Application

This cockpit transformed quarterly commercial reviews from subjective pricing debates into rigorous mathematical scenario evaluations.

The Cost of Bad Procurement Timing

In heavy manufacturing (steel rerolling, construction infrastructure), raw material procurement represents over 70% of total Cost of Goods Sold (COGS). Purchasing 5,000 metric tons of steel billet 2 weeks too early during a cyclical peak can wipe out an entire quarter's operating profit.


Engineering the Steel Intelligence Cockpit

To empower procurement directors with actionable foresight, we designed the Steel Price Intelligence Cockpit:

  • Index Consolidation: Tracks international scrap benchmarks, billet import parity, and domestic rebar price spreads in a unified telemetry stream.
  • Technical Volatility Bands: Uses rolling 30-day and 90-day moving averages and Bollinger volatility bands to detect overbought market conditions.
  • Single-File Portable Architecture: Engineered to run with zero dependencies for rapid deployment in boardroom discussions and trading floors.

Key Commercial Takeaway

Commodity intelligence is not about predicting the future with certainty—it is about avoiding high-risk buying zones and systematically locking in favorable conversion margins.

Agro-feed and agricultural input businesses operate under unique macroeconomic dynamics: seasonal crop harvest cycles, localized weather risks, and complex dealer credit terms. Econometric Methodology & Findings

Using Python (Pandas, Statsmodels) and Advanced Excel regression modeling across 200 student records:

  • Diminishing Marginal Returns: After 25 weekly study hours, marginal score gains tapered significantly, highlighting the importance of study efficiency over brute-force cramming.

blogs.title: Why Average Ratings Lie: Dissecting 9,551 Zomato Restaurants & Simpson's Paradox
blogs.snippet: Unweighted country averages mislead decision makers. Analyzing 9,551 Zomato restaurants revealed that 22.5% of listings are unrated, with 2,139 of those concentrated in a single nation...
blogs.content:
The Deception of Simple Averages

When analyzing large commercial datasets, aggregating ratings into a simple arithmetic mean across countries frequently introduces severe aggregation bias (Simpson's Paradox). Without inspecting the distribution, analysts reach deeply flawed conclusions.


Key Exploratory Findings Across 9,551 Restaurants

Utilizing Python, Pandas, Matplotlib, and Seaborn, the audit revealed:

  • The Zero-Rating Distortion: 22.5% of all restaurant listings (2,148 venues) possessed a 0.0 rating because they were unrated, with 2,139 located in India alone. Including these in national averages dragged India's mean rating artificially low.
  • Online Delivery vs. Table Booking: Venues offering online delivery demonstrated significantly higher rating frequencies than dine-in-only establishments.
  • Price Tier Elasticity: High-end tier 4 venues maintained tight rating variance, while mid-tier venues displayed volatile customer sentiment.

blogs.title: Pareto in the Kitchen: Auditing 1,000 Fast-Food Orders for Revenue Concentration & Payment Gaps
blogs.snippet: Three menu items carry 64.6% of total franchise revenue, while 11.6% of orders lack payment records. Learn how Python Pandas exploratory analysis exposed retail revenue friction...

The Operational Friction in Quick-Service Restaurants (QSR)

Fast-food franchises operate on razor-thin net margins. Even small discrepancies in POS registration, peak kitchen prep bottlenecks, and payment gateway drops can turn a profitable month into a loss.


Audit Insights from 1,000 Transactions

Executing systematic exploratory data analysis with Python Pandas uncovered:

  • Extreme Pareto Revenue Concentration: Just three menu items accounted for 64.6% of gross franchise revenue, suggesting that 60% of the long-tail menu could be streamlined to reduce kitchen prep overhead.
  • 11.6% Unrecorded Payment Anomaly: 116 out of 1,000 order transactions contained missing or unrecorded payment method identifiers, flagging potential floor shrinkage and terminal sync failures.
  • Hourly Rush Hour Clustering: 72% of order volume concentrated in two distinct 90-minute lunch and evening surges, dictating optimal staff scheduling.
